docs.title: Your first minute
docs.text:
Prompt
Use rup-flow to document this system in docs/rup, in English:
an online shop where customers place orders for products.

The agent asks only what it cannot know, writes the documents, draws the diagrams and checks the result. Open docs/rup/README.md and follow the links.

Current documentation: this site describes rup-flow 1.0 (free) and rup-flow Pro 1.0. Use the version selector when you operate another release line so commands and configuration match the skill you installed. How versions map

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
rup-flow is a skill plus a small command line. The skill tells an AI coding agent what to do and what never to do; the command line does the work that must be exact: creating structure, keeping an index in sync, drawing diagrams and checking the result. There is no service, no account and no dependency to install beyond Node.js 18.

This section explains how the pieces fit, in the order a newcomer needs them.

docs.title: The shape in one picture
docs.text: The person never talks to rup-flow directly. They talk to an agent. The agent reads the rules of the skill, runs the CLI for the mechanical steps and writes the documents itself, because understanding a business is the part that needs a language model. Each side does what it is good at, and the boundary between them is a plain command line that any agent with a shell can use.

docs.title: Principles
docs.text: Principle What it means in practice One portable core The skill follows the open Agent Skills format. Anything specific to one agent lives in a small adapter and never in the skill The agent analyses, the CLI does the boilerplate Structure, indexes, rendering and checks are deterministic code; judgement stays with the agent Honesty over completeness The rules forbid inventing content, and the CLI refuses what an edition does not include instead of faking it Nothing to install Node.js 18 or newer is enough; Docker only draws diagrams Two editions, one code base The free CLI loads an extension when it finds one; there is no fork

docs.title: Runtime behaviour
docs.text: Three scenarios show how the pieces cooperate. Each one is a rule you can rely on.

docs.title: Adding a use case
docs.text:
1. The person states the use case in plain language.
  2. The agent runs new use-case with what it knows: actor, package, goal.
  3. The CLI chooses the next free identifier by reading the existing cards, writes only the files that do not exist yet, and regenerates the index from the cards.
  4. The agent fills the card from what the person said. Whatever the person did not say becomes an open question.
  5. The agent runs check and reports the files, the open questions and what was not checked.

Two properties follow. Running the command twice never overwrites work, because existing files are skipped. And the index is always derived from the cards, never edited by hand.

docs.title: Rendering diagrams
docs.text:
• A diagram is up to date when its SVG is newer than its source; --force redraws everything, and a change of palette does so automatically.
  • A failure of one diagram never stops the others. The report lists what was drawn, what was skipped and what failed, and the exit code is 1 when anything failed.
  • The SVG is written to a temporary file and moved into place, so an interrupted run never leaves half an image.

docs.title: Starting the CLI
docs.text: The edition is decided once, at start, by one file. A command that needs Pro never half-runs in the free edition: it stops before doing any work and says which part is missing.

docs.title: The report
docs.text: Every command ends with a report: a title, then labelled values and lists. The same shape is used by all commands so an agent can read any of them the same way.

docs.title: Qualities
docs.text: Quality How it is protected Portability The skill follows the open Agent Skills format; adapters isolate each agent; the CLI needs only Node.js Honesty Provenance marks, the rule against inventing content, open questions, and a CLI that refuses what the edition lacks Repeatability Commands skip what exists, derive indexes from the cards, and record the render state Safety Writes only inside chosen folders; local, sandboxed rendering; no network calls of its own Maintainability One reason to change per module; a catalogue and validation that stop the editions drifting Compatibility One CLI and one skill structure for both editions, so a project moves from free to Pro without renaming

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text: Each decision states the context, the choice and what it costs.

docs.title: D-01 A skill plus a CLI, not a skill alone
docs.text: Context. An agent writes good prose and bad boilerplate: it renumbers identifiers, forgets to refresh an index, draws diagrams it cannot see. Decision. Mechanical work is deterministic code behind a command line; judgement stays with the agent. Cost. The agent must be able to run a command; an agent that cannot, writes documents without rendering or checking and must say so.

docs.title: D-02 No runtime dependencies
docs.text: Context. The skill is unzipped into any folder on any machine. Decision. The CLI uses only the Node.js standard library. Cost. Small utilities are written in the project instead of imported.

docs.title: D-03 PlantUML in a local container, not a hosted service
docs.text: Context. Diagrams describe private systems. Decision. Rendering goes to a container on the loopback interface, with a sandboxed profile. Cost. Docker is needed to draw; without it the sources are still written and can be drawn later.

docs.title: D-04 One CLI, two editions, selected by a file
docs.text: Context. Forking the code for a paid edition doubles every fix. Decision. The free CLI loads an extension when it finds scripts/pro/index.mjs; the Pro package is the free skill with an overlay. Cost. The free tree must expose clean extension points and stay free of Pro code, which validation enforces.

docs.title: D-05 Refuse, do not degrade
docs.text: Context. A free edition that quietly produces a weaker version of a Pro artifact would mislead. Decision. Anything outside the edition stops with a message that names Pro, or is counted and listed; the skill tells the agent not to improvise it. Cost. Some requests end earlier than a user expects, which is the point.

docs.title: D-06 Numbered folders that never change
docs.text: Context. Users move from free to Pro. Decision. Both editions use the same discipline folders; Pro fills the rest. Cost. The free tree shows folders that Pro uses and the free edition leaves empty or absent.

docs.title: D-07 Light and dark diagrams are two files
docs.text: Context. One SVG cannot be readable on both a white and a dark page. Decision. Documentation diagrams are drawn twice from one source with two palettes and the page shows the one that matches its theme. Cost. Twice the files, checked as a pair by the build.

docs.title: D-08 Instruction files for agents without skills
docs.text: Context. Many agents read a rules file instead of Agent Skills. Decision. A command writes a small, delimited block into the file each tool reads and replaces only that block. Cost. The list of targets follows each tool's conventions and needs maintenance.

docs.title: One repository, two branches
docs.text:
The source lives in one private repository with two long-lived branches. The packages built from them are what is published; the source is not.

Branch Holds Tag Package main The free edition vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH rup-flow-free-<version>.zip pro main plus the pro/ folder: overlay, build, tests, license pro-vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH rup-flow-pro-<version>.zip

main is complete and never contains anything from Pro. After a change lands in main it is merged into pro, so the Pro build always contains a known free version, and the Pro package states it. Both branches only take changes through pull requests with CI complete.

docs.title: From change to package
docs.text:
Job Checks Validate Skill format, links, no sensitive-looking names, no Pro templates in the free tree Test The CLI suite on Linux and Windows with Node.js 18 and 22 Render init, new use-case, render and check against a real PlantUML server Pro tests The built Pro skill: every command, the explorer, the example project and the package

The release workflow checks that the tag equals the version in the files, runs the tests, builds the package and attaches it to the GitHub release with the changelog section as its notes. A release is never overwritten.

docs.title: Version identity
docs.text: A package names its version in three places that must agree: the file name, SKILL.md metadata and the output of RUP version. Pro also names the free version it contains. See Versioning and URLs.

docs.title: Editions and the extension point
docs.text: There is one CLI. Which edition you run depends on one file.

docs.title: Assembly
docs.text: The free package is the free skill, zipped. The Pro package is a copy of the free skill with the Pro overlay laid over it and the folder renamed rup-flow-pro. Files in the overlay replace files of the same path, which is how Pro swaps a short template for its full version without a second code path. The build also records the Pro version and the free version it contains.

docs.title: Detection
docs.text:
At start, the CLI looks for scripts/pro/index.mjs next to itself:

File present Edition Behaviour No Free Runs on its own. Anything outside the edition stops with a message that names Pro Yes Pro The extension adds capabilities and the CLI uses them

docs.title: What the extension adds
docs.text:
The extension is a module that the CLI calls at defined points:

Point Free behaviour With the extension Templates Only the free templates exist; init and new use-case skip the rest and count them The remaining templates are present and are written Rendering Default PlantUML look Palettes, Mermaid, PNG previews Use-case index A table A table and the use-case diagrams Commands The free commands Plus themes, explore and scan Configuration A Mermaid language or a non-svg output is rejected Accepted Instructions Lists the free commands Lists all commands Version Reports the free version Reports the Pro version and the free version it contains

docs.title: The catalogue
docs.text: editions.json lists every diagram, document, workflow and tool with its tier. RUP editions prints it and marks what the installation includes. The comparison page of this site is generated from the same list, so the CLI and the documentation cannot disagree.

docs.title: Rules for contributors
docs.text:
• A capability that is not in the free edition stops with a message that names Pro and exits with code 1, or appears in the available in Pro line. It never fails silently and is never reimplemented in the free tree.
  • Every new artifact gets an entry in editions.json.
  • Validation rejects Pro templates inside the free skill.
  • Behaviour specific to one edition is selected by the presence of the extension, never by a setting a user could flip.

docs.title: What runs where
docs.text:
Everything runs on your machine. There are three runtime pieces and two stores.

Element Responsibility Agent process Reads SKILL.md and the references, decides what to write, runs the CLI and writes the documents Node.js process One short-lived run per CLI command: structure, index, render, check, instructions Skill folder Rules, references, templates, the catalogue and the CLI itself; read-only at run time Project folder rup.config.json and the documentation directory; the only place the tool writes PlantUML container Turns diagram sources into SVG; published on 127.0.0.1 only and run with the SANDBOX security profile

The CLI is started fresh for every command and keeps no state between runs, except one small file in the documentation directory that records the last render so unchanged diagrams are skipped.

docs.text: Component Responsibility Reason it is separate Argument parser Splits a command line into the command, its arguments and flags The only place that knows the shape of the command line Configuration loader Merges defaults, rup.config.json and flags, in that order of precedence, and rejects values the edition does not support Every command sees one resolved configuration Commands One function per command A command can change without touching the others edition.mjs Detects the edition, loads the extension, prints Pro notices The single point where the two editions differ usecases.mjs Reads the use-case cards and builds the index and the navigation Shared by new use-case, index and check plantuml.mjs Sends a source to the server and checks that an SVG came back The only code that speaks HTTP instructions.mjs Writes the block that agents without skills read Isolates the list of agent targets scripts/pro Themes, Mermaid, explorer, use-case diagrams and code scan Exists only in the Pro package

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text: The CLI has no runtime dependencies. It uses the Node.js standard library, the global fetch for the PlantUML server and, only when asked, the docker command. Keeping the dependency list empty is a requirement, not an accident: it is what lets the skill be unzipped into any folder and run.

docs.title: Trust and data flow
docs.text: rup-flow has no account, no analytics and no service of its own. This page lists every boundary it touches.

docs.title: On your machine
docs.text:
It does Where Reads and writes files Inside the folders you point it at: the documentation directory and rup.config.json Sends diagram sources To the PlantUML server you run locally, http://127.0.0.1:8085 by default Pulls a container image The PlantUML image from its public registry, the first time you start the server

Nothing else is sent anywhere. rup-flow Pro adds one more image, the Mermaid renderer, pulled the first time you choose Mermaid.

docs.title: The agent
docs.text: The AI agent you use with the skill processes your prompts and the files it reads under its provider's terms and privacy policy, not rup-flow's. rup-flow cannot see or limit that. Choose an agent whose terms fit the material you document.

docs.title: The PlantUML container
docs.text: The bundled compose file publishes the container on 127.0.0.1 only and runs it with the SANDBOX security profile, which blocks file and address access from diagrams. Do not expose that port to a network without adding authentication. The CLI never uses an !include of a file or an address in the sources it writes.

docs.title: Written output
docs.text: Generated documentation contains whatever you or the code contain. Review it before you publish it, especially output derived from code in rup-flow Pro: paths, configuration and table names.

docs.title: The explorer Pro
docs.text: explorer.html carries a content security policy that blocks every external load, and inserts diagrams and documents as nodes, never as raw HTML. It can be shared as a file.

docs.title: Reporting a vulnerability
docs.text: Report vulnerabilities privately to the maintainer; do not open a public issue. The security policy explains where.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
rup.config.json sits in the project root. init creates it; every key is optional because the defaults below apply.

rup.config.json
{
  "project": "my-project",
  "outDir": "docs/rup",
  "docLanguage": "en",
  "codeRoot": "src",
  "paths": {
    "domain": "00-domain-model",
    "requirements": "01-requirements",
    "analysis": "02-analysis",
    "design": "03-design",
    "implementation": "04-implementation",
    "quality": "05-quality"
  },
  "useCaseDir": "use-cases",
  "plantuml": { "url": "http://127.0.0.1:8085", "timeoutMs": 30000 },
  "diagrams": { "language": "plantuml", "outputs": ["svg"] },
  "ids": { "requirement": "RF", "nonFunctional": "RNF", "useCase": "UC", "rule": "RN", "decision": "DEC", "test": "TC" },
  "targetStack": { "language": "", "framework": "", "persistence": "", "testing": "" }
}

docs.title: Precedence
docs.text:
Flags override the file, and the file overrides the defaults:

flags  >  rup.config.json  >  defaults

config prints the resolved result.

docs.title: Changing paths on an existing project
docs.text: Changing paths or outDir after documents exist means moving the folders and fixing the links. Do it as one explicit step and run check afterwards.

docs.title: Pro settings in the free edition
docs.text: The free edition does not ignore a Pro setting silently. A Mermaid language or a non-svg output in the file, or any --theme, --font, --color-* or --preview-png flag, stops the command with a message that names Pro. theme and mermaid keys are only read by Pro.

docs.title: The documentation
docs.text:
This site lives in rup-flow-docs, the only public repository of the project. Work on a branch, run npm run verify and open a pull request.

Rules that keep the site honest:

  • Document released behaviour. The free edition and rup-flow Pro are both documented; mark every page, table row or step that belongs to Pro with edition: pro in the front matter or the Pro tag.
  • Never document behaviour that does not exist, and never promise a roadmap item as if it shipped.
  • Examples contain no credentials or private data.
  • Diagrams are PlantUML sources in docs/assets/diagrams/sources, drawn in a light and a dark look; edit the source, never the SVG.

docs.title: The skill
docs.text: The skill source is private; it is distributed as the free and Pro packages. Report a problem in the skill, or a client that ignores the instruction files, in the documentation repository's issues with the documentation template and say which edition and version (RUP version) you use.

docs.title: Reporting a problem
docs.text: Open an issue with the documentation template. Report vulnerabilities privately as described in the security policy.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text: All diagrams follow the same conventions.

docs.title: Analysis classes
docs.text: The first software structure derived from the use cases: what the user touches (boundary), what coordinates (control) and what holds information (entity).

docs.title: Source
docs.text:
@startuml
!theme plain
hide empty members
skinparam linetype polyline
top to bottom direction

class CheckoutScreen <<boundary>>
class CreateOrderController <<control>>
class Order <<entity>>
class OrderLine <<entity>>
class Product <<entity>>
class Customer <<entity>>

CheckoutScreen --> CreateOrderController
CreateOrderController --> Order
CreateOrderController --> Product
CreateOrderController --> Customer
Order *-- OrderLine
OrderLine --> Product

@enduml

docs.title: Stereotypes
docs.text: Stereotype Role <<boundary>> Interface between the actor and the system: a screen, an endpoint <<control>> Coordination of one use case <<entity>> Domain information, taken from the domain model

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Arrows point down, from boundary to control to entity.
  • One control class per use case.
  • Entity names are the ones in the domain model.

In Pro

Pro adds one analysis collaboration per use case, with numbered messages, and the analysis card that links it to the requirements and the design.

docs.title: Header
docs.text:
Every PlantUML source starts the same way:

@startuml
!theme plain
hide empty members
hide circle
skinparam linetype polyline

Use top to bottom direction by default. Use left to right direction only for short linear flows of four elements or fewer: wide diagrams shrink to unreadable text when embedded.

docs.title: No colors in sources
docs.text: The free edition renders with the default PlantUML look. Do not write colors or theme blocks into sources. Palettes are a Pro feature applied when the diagram is drawn, so the sources stay clean.

docs.title: Avoiding collisions
docs.text:
1. Keep each diagram to twelve to fifteen elements. Split into views before squeezing.
  2. Group related elements in a package.
  3. Fix the order of elements with hidden links, for example A -[hidden]right-> B.
  4. Hold elements together or apart with together { … } and skinparam nodesep or ranksep between 50 and 80.
  5. Prefer short relation labels; put long text in notes on elements.
  6. Write relations with a direction (Order *-down- OrderLine). A plain -- lets both ends land on the same row.
  7. Avoid relations from one hub to everything; introduce a package.
  8. If lines still cross badly after two adjustments, split the diagram.

docs.title: Sandbox
docs.text: The PlantUML server runs with the SANDBOX profile. Diagrams must not use !include of files or addresses.

docs.title: Naming
docs.text: PlantUML identifiers are English, without spaces (use as), and equal to the names in the model. A title inside a diagram is optional; the Markdown heading names the diagram.

docs.title: Simplified domain model
docs.text: The business concepts of the project and the relations between them. Attributes and importance levels are left out; the entity dictionary carries the detail.

docs.title: Source
docs.text:
@startuml
!theme plain
hide empty members
hide circle
skinparam linetype polyline
top to bottom direction

class Order
class Customer
class OrderLine
class Product
class Address

Order *-- OrderLine
Customer -- Order
OrderLine --> Product
Order --> Address

@enduml

docs.title: How to draw it
docs.text:
• File 00-domain-model/domain-model-simple.puml.
  • Entities and relations only. Choose each relation by meaning: composition only when the part cannot live without the whole.
  • Keep it to twelve entities or fewer; split before squeezing.
  • Names are the business terms recorded in the entity dictionary.

docs.title: Companion documents
docs.text:
00-domain-model/README.md holds the entity dictionary (definition, key attributes, source) and the business rules (RN-xxx).

In Pro

Pro draws the same model ranked by importance, with attributes and multiplicities, and adds the lifecycle of the entities whose state changes behaviour. See the catalogue.

docs.title: Use-case specification
docs.text: The specification is the behaviour source of truth of a use case: a statechart of the conversation between the actor and the system. The card describes the same paths in words; if they diverge, the specification wins and the card is corrected.

docs.title: Source
docs.text:
@startuml
!theme plain
skinparam linetype polyline
hide empty description

state "createOrder" as createOrder {
  state " " as Basket
  state " " as Checkout
  state " " as Validating
  state " " as Placed

  [*] --> Basket
  Basket --> Checkout : Customer checks out
  Checkout --> Validating : Customer confirms
  Validating --> Checkout : System reports a problem
  Validating --> Placed : System creates the order
  Placed --> [*]

  note on link
    Actor: asks to check out
    System: shows lines, totals and the address form
  end note
}

@enduml

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• A composite state named after the use case; inner states have no visible label.
  • Transitions are the events of the conversation.
  • Notes on transitions narrate what the actor does and what the system answers.
  • Error and cancel paths are explicit transitions.
  • skinparam linetype polyline.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• The main flow reaches the goal and every step has a system response.
  • Every input and every precondition has a failure path.
  • The paths match the flows in the card.

In Pro

Pro adds the wireframes of the screens of the flow, the analysis collaboration and the design sequence for the same use case, each linked from the card. See the catalogue.

docs.title: Compatible agents
docs.text: rup-flow does not depend on one agent. It reaches them in three ways.

docs.title: 1. The agent reads Agent Skills
docs.text: The skill follows the open Agent Skills format. A client that reads it loads SKILL.md and the references on demand. Put the folder where the client looks for skills (installation).

docs.title: 2. The agent reads an instruction file
docs.text:
Tools that read a rules file get a small block that points them at the skill. The instructions command writes it, replaces it between its markers when you run it again and never touches the rest of the file:

node scripts/rup.mjs instructions --target cursor,windsurf --root .

docs.title: 3. Any other agent with a shell
docs.text:
An agent that can read a file and run a command can use rup-flow. Write the portable file, tell the agent to read it, and it follows the same rules and runs the same CLI:

Prompt

docs.title: What every agent must be able to do
docs.text:
Capability Why Read files and the skill folder The rules and references are plain Markdown Run node The CLI is a Node.js program Write files The documents are Markdown and PlantUML

An agent that cannot run commands can still write the documents by following the references, but it cannot render or check them; it must say so.

docs.title: What is tested
docs.text: The automated tests check that every target writes its file, keeps the rest of an existing file, does not duplicate its block, and that the skill installs into both skill folders. What an agent does with the files is up to the agent; report a client that ignores them.

docs.title: The prompt
docs.text:
Prompt
Use rup-flow to document this system in docs/rup, in English:
an online shop where customers place orders for products.
Actor: Customer. Requirement RF-001: a customer can place an order for one or
more products. Rules: an order has at least one line; a line quantity cannot
exceed stock.

The more you state, the less the agent has to ask. What you do not state is marked assumed or goes to the open questions.

docs.title: What happens
docs.text:
1. The agent reads rup.config.json, or runs init to create it.
  2. It lists the gaps. Blocking questions (rules that change the model) are asked; the rest are marked.
  3. It writes the domain model, actors, requirements, the use case and the analysis classes.
  4. It renders the diagrams and runs check.
  5. It reports files created, open questions, checks that were not executed and the next step.

docs.text:
docs/rup/
├── README.md
├── 00-domain-model/   README.md, domain-model-simple.puml/.svg
├── 01-requirements/   README.md, actors.md, requirements.md, use-cases/createOrder/

docs.title: Check it yourself
docs.text:
node scripts/rup.mjs check --root .

Past the first minute: when you ask for design, traceability or code, the agent tells you plainly that it is part of rup-flow Pro and does not invent it.

docs.title: The skill
docs.text:
SKILL.md holds the operating rules and tells the agent which reference to read for each request. The references (methodology, domain-model, use-cases, diagram-conventions, structure) are loaded on demand so the agent spends its attention on your project, not on boilerplate.

The skill is written once in the open Agent Skills format. Agents that do not read that format read a small instruction file instead; see Compatible agents.

docs.title: The CLI
docs.text:
A dependency-free Node.js program does the mechanical work:

It does Command Creates the structure and the configuration init, new use-case Keeps the use-case index in sync with the cards index Draws .puml sources into .svg render Verifies structure, links and diagrams check Writes the block that agents without skills read instructions Tells what is installed version, editions

docs.title: The operating rules
docs.text:
1. Read the configuration first.
  2. Mark every statement as confirmed, assumed or open.
  3. Never invent permissions, rules, states or attributes.
  4. Write where the configuration says.
  5. Do not claim a diagram is rendered or checked unless it was.
  6. Write documents in your language; keep identifiers in English.
  7. Keep one source of truth per artifact.

See Provenance marks and the architecture.

docs.title: Editions
docs.text: The same CLI runs both editions. rup-flow Pro adds an extension that the CLI loads when it is present; without it, the CLI is the free edition and says so when you ask for something outside it. Read Editions and the extension point.

docs.title: Install rup-flow
docs.text: Both editions are one folder, rup-flow (free) or rup-flow-pro (Pro), that you place where your agent looks for skills. They are the same skill: install one of them in a given place, not both.

docs.title: Check the runtime

node --version

The skill needs Node.js 18 or newer. Docker is only needed to draw diagrams (see Render and check diagrams).

docs.title: Get the package

docs.title: 1. State the objective
docs.text: One sentence: what the system is for and for whom. The agent restates it before modelling; correct it there.

docs.title: 2. Answer the blocking questions
docs.text: The agent separates questions that change the model (a rule, an actor, a state) from details. It asks the first kind and continues with the rest marked assumed. Anything you do not answer stays in 05-quality/open-questions.md.

docs.title: 3. Review the domain model
docs.text: Open 00-domain-model/README.md. Check the entity dictionary and the business rules. A rule marked assumed is a question for you, not a decision.

docs.title: 4. Review the requirements
docs.text: 01-requirements/requirements.md lists functional (RF-xxx) and non-functional (RNF-xxx) requirements with their origin and who confirmed them. Each RF should have at least one use case, and each use case at least one RF.

docs.title: 5. Review each use case
docs.text: Open the card. Check the main flow, alternative flows, preconditions and postconditions. Open specification.svg: the card and the diagram must describe the same paths; if they diverge, the specification wins.

docs.title: 6. Mark what is reviewed
docs.text: Change status in the front matter from draft to reviewed for the artifacts you accepted. The agent never promotes an artifact on its own.

docs.title: 7. Check
docs.text: node scripts/rup.mjs check --root .

docs.title: Where the free edition stops
docs.text: Design (classes, sequences, data model, deployment), implementation cards, traceability and audits belong to rup-flow Pro.

docs.title: Start the server
docs.text:
Diagrams are PlantUML sources. A local Docker container draws them:

node scripts/rup.mjs server up --root .
node scripts/rup.mjs health --root .

health renders a test diagram and prints OK when the server is usable. Stop the server with server down.

The container publishes its port on 127.0.0.1 only and runs with the SANDBOX security profile, which blocks file and URL access from diagrams.

docs.title: Render
docs.text:
node scripts/rup.mjs render --root .

Each name.puml becomes name.svg next to it. Up-to-date diagrams are skipped; use --force to redraw everything, or --path <dir> to render one folder. A file with several @start…/@end… blocks produces name-01.svg, name-02.svg.

docs.title: Check
docs.text:
node scripts/rup.mjs check --root .
Message Meaning Fix broken link A Markdown link points to a file that does not exist Fix the link or create the file unbalanced @start/@end A diagram source is cut off Complete the source no rendered SVG A source has no image yet Run render use-case index is stale A card changed since the index was generated Run index unresolved template placeholder A {{name}} is still in a document Fill it in

check --strict turns warnings into a failing exit code, which suits CI.

docs.title: What check does not do
docs.text: It validates structure and links. It does not prove that UML is semantically correct or that lines do not cross. Look at the rendered images.

docs.title: The server is not reachable
docs.text: PlantUML server not usable at http://127.0.0.1:8085. Start Docker, then run server up and health. If the port is taken, change plantuml.url in rup.config.json (the port in it is the one the container publishes).

docs.title: docker compose failed. Is Docker running?
docs.text: Docker Desktop or the Docker daemon is stopped. Start it and retry.

docs.title: A diagram fails to render
docs.text: PlantUML reported a syntax error in this diagram names the file in the render report. Fix the source; do not paste colors or !include lines, the server is sandboxed.

docs.title: ... is part of rup-flow Pro
docs.text: You asked for something this edition does not include: a theme, Mermaid, PNG previews, the explorer, scan and the Pro documents. The message includes the address of the Pro page. See Free and Pro compared.

docs.title: Output directory not found
docs.text: check needs the structure first. Run init.

docs.title: The agent invents things
docs.text: Remind it of the rules: mark every statement as confirmed, assumed or open, and send unknown rules to open-questions.md. If it improvises past what the free edition provides, tell it to name what is missing instead.

docs.title: Paths with spaces on Windows
docs.text: Quote them: --root "C:\My Projects\shop".

docs.title: Add one
docs.text:
Ask the agent: "Add the use case cancelOrder for the Customer", or run:

node scripts/rup.mjs new use-case cancelOrder --title "Cancel order" --actor Customer --package Ordering --goal "Cancel an order that has not shipped" --root .

The command creates the card and the specification diagram, assigns the next UC-xxx identifier and refreshes the index. Names are camelCase: verb plus object.

Flag Meaning --title Human title of the card --actor One or several actors, comma separated --package Group of related use cases --goal The user goal in one sentence --requirement Requirement identifier, RF-001 by default --includes, --extends Names of related use cases

docs.title: Keep the index fresh
docs.text:
The requirements README.md holds a generated table between the markers rup-flow:use-cases. After editing the front matter of a card, run:

node scripts/rup.mjs index --root .

Never edit the block by hand: check warns when it is stale.

docs.title: Write a good card
docs.text:
• One user goal per use case, achievable in one sitting by one primary actor.
  • Flows are tables with Actor and System columns; one step is one interaction.
  • Every alternative flow names the step where it starts, its condition and where it ends.
  • Postconditions are split into success and failure.
  • Anything you did not state goes to Pending with the question.

docs.title: Keep card and specification together
docs.text: The specification is a statechart of the Actor/System conversation. Error and cancel paths are explicit transitions. See Use-case specification.

docs.title: Code to RUP
docs.text:
Point the agent at a code base and ask for its documentation. Pro writes the same documentation set as for a new system, but every statement describes what the code does, marked observed and cited as path:line. The artifacts carry origin: code and sourceOfTruth: code.

Prompt
Use rup-flow-pro to reverse engineer src/ into docs/rup, in English.

docs.title: The procedure
docs.text:
1. Inventory. RUP scan --code-root <dir> --write lists the manifests, entry points, entities, services, persistence, contracts and tests, so the agent starts from facts.
  2. Stack and architecture. Identified from manifests and folder layout and recorded in the project configuration document.
  3. Domain model. Persistence first (schema, migrations, ORM models), then entity classes. One entity per business concept, not per table: join and technical tables are support entities or omitted with a note.
  4. Levels. The agent asks for the project objective, or infers it from the README and the entry points and marks it assumed, then assigns the levels.
  5. Use cases. Derived from the entry points: each route, command handler, job, message consumer or CLI command that achieves a user goal. Technical endpoints that serve one goal become one use case.
  6. Specification. The agent follows the code path of each use case: validation, branching, errors, side effects. The statechart shows only behaviour found in code. A branch that cannot be understood is an open question, not a guess.
  7. Analysis and design. Classes, sequences, data model and deployment are drawn from the real call graph, the configuration and the deployment files (Dockerfile, compose, CI, infrastructure as code).
  8. Code map and traceability. Every model element gets its location; the code column of the traceability table is filled.
  9. Tests. Existing tests fill the test column; use cases without tests are gaps.
  10. Render, check, review.

docs.title: Rules the agent follows
docs.text:
• It writes behaviour, not intent. Intent that the code does not reveal, such as why a rule exists, is a question.
  • Dead code, TODOs and inconsistent behaviour are findings in the audit, not silent fixes in the model.
  • It cites path:line instead of pasting code.
  • It reads files fully before describing them; it never describes from names alone.
  • On large code bases it works module by module and keeps a coverage list of what was and was not read.

docs.title: What you get at the end
docs.text: The files created, the entities and use cases found, the parts not covered and the open questions. Statements it could not support are never presented as facts.

docs.title: Domain model diagrams
docs.text: The free edition draws entities and relations. Pro draws the same model ranked by importance, with the attributes that matter and the multiplicity of every relation, and adds the lifecycle of the entities whose state changes behaviour.

docs.title: Ranked domain model
docs.text:
• One package per level, level 1 on top, tagged so the palette colors the bands.
  • Relations point downwards where the meaning allows; a relation that points upwards is legitimate but is a signal to re-check the levels.
  • Multiplicities on every relation, and composition only when the part cannot live without the whole.
  • Attributes that carry business meaning or that a use case needs. Trivial ones are omitted and the README says so in an "omitted attributes and why" column.
  • Hidden links hold the order of the bands and of the entities inside one band, so the diagram reads the same after every change.

docs.title: Entity lifecycles
docs.text: Only entities whose state changes behaviour get one. Each transition names the use case that causes it, so the lifecycle and the use cases cannot drift apart.

docs.title: Related
docs.text: The complete documentation set · Themes · Diagram conventions

docs.title: Use-case diagram
docs.text:
• Actors stay outside the system boundary; packages group related use cases inside it.
  • include and extend relations come from the front matter of the cards.
  • An actor is linked only to the use cases that no other use case of that actor includes.
  • It is regenerated by RUP index from the cards: never edit it by hand.

docs.title: One diagram per actor
docs.text: When there are several actors, Pro also draws a diagram per actor with only the use cases that actor triggers, plus the ones they include or extend.

docs.title: Wireframes
docs.text:
• One sketch per screen of the flow, drawn as a PlantUML salt layout so it stays text.
  • Every field shown maps to a domain attribute or a parameter of the use case; every attribute the use case needs appears in some screen.
  • Wireframes are PlantUML also when the project uses Mermaid, because Mermaid has no wireframe diagram.

docs.title: The complete documentation set
docs.text:
Pro writes all six disciplines into the same numbered folders the free edition uses, so a project moves to Pro without renaming anything. Each artifact has a front matter that records its identifier, status, origin and source of truth; see Front matter and identifiers.

Discipline Free Pro adds 00-domain-model Simplified model, dictionary, rules Ranked model, levels, attributes, multiplicities, entity lifecycles 01-requirements Actors, requirements, use-case card, specification Use-case diagrams, wireframes, navigation between cards 02-analysis Analysis classes Collaboration per use case, analysis card 03-design none Design classes, sequence per use case, data model, components, deployment, project configuration 04-implementation none Code map, implementation and tests card per use case 05-quality Open questions Project profile, traceability, audit, decision records

docs.title: 00 Domain model
docs.text:
The model is organised in four horizontal bands. The higher the band, the more central the entity is to the project objective written in the project profile.

Level Meaning Test 1 Core The reason the project exists Without it the objective is not met 2 Structural Depend directly on level 1 and give it shape Cannot exist or make sense without a level-1 entity 3 Detail Qualify, specialise or break down level 2 Removing it loses precision, not purpose 4 Support Catalogues, audit, configuration Replaceable without changing the business meaning
  • The README justifies the levels for the project. The same concept can be level 1 in one project and level 4 in another.
  • Position is a reading aid: it never implies inheritance or composition.
  • At most three to five entities per level; a band that grows is split into a sub-model with the simple model kept as the map.
  • Only entities whose state changes behaviour get a lifecycle diagram, and each transition names the use case that causes it.

See Domain model diagrams.

docs.title: 01 Requirements
docs.text:
• The use-case diagram groups use cases in packages inside the system boundary, with actors outside it; include and extend come from the cards' front matter. A separate diagram is drawn per actor when there are several.
  • Every use case has a wireframe for each screen of its flow. Every field shown maps to a domain attribute or a parameter of the use case.

See Requirements diagrams and Use-case cards.

docs.title: 02 Analysis
docs.text: One collaboration per use case: the actor, the boundary it uses, the control that coordinates and the entities touched, with numbered messages. Boundaries talk only to controls, controls talk to entities and other controls, entities never call upward.

docs.title: 03 Design
docs.text:
Design classes and their operations, a sequence per use case with its failure path and transaction boundary, the data model with its mapping from entities, the components with the interfaces they provide and require, the deployment, and the project configuration (stack, build, run, environment variables). Each non-obvious choice becomes a decision record. The use-case design card lists the design elements that realize it, which is what RUP to code reads.

See Analysis and design diagrams.

docs.title: 04 Implementation
docs.text: The code map lists every model element and its location. Each use case has a card with the code and the tests that implement it.

docs.title: 05 Quality
docs.text: Artifact Holds Project profile Objective, scope, constraints, stack, who confirms what Traceability Requirement, use case, analysis, design, code and test, one row per use case Open questions Every unknown, who asked, what it blocks Audit Findings with evidence, severity, impact and fix, and the checks not executed Decision records One DEC-xxx per decision and its reasons

docs.title: Consistency rules
docs.text:
• The models are the single source of truth for what they describe, unless an artifact says sourceOfTruth: code.
  • A change in one artifact is propagated to the dependent ones, and the traceability table is updated in the same change.
  • Every requirement has at least one use case; every use case has at least one requirement.
  • check reports gaps: a use case without realization, an empty code or test cell, a row missing from the traceability table.

docs.text: The Pro package ships a complete example, an online shop, with every artifact above.

docs.title: Domain libraries
docs.text:
A domain library is a starting point for a project whose objective matches a known domain: a ranked domain model, actors, a list of use cases, the entity lifecycles and the questions to ask before using it. Libraries live in the domains folder of the Pro skill.

Everything in a library is marked assumed. The agent adapts it to your objective, asks you to confirm each rule and moves what is not confirmed to the open questions. It never presents a library as your requirements.

docs.title: lms
docs.text: The agent offers it when the objective mentions courses, enrolment, learners and teachers, activities, grading or completion.

docs.title: Entities
docs.text: Entity Level Definition Enrolment 1 A learner's participation in a course Course 1 A taught unit with sections and activities Learner 2 Person who takes courses Teacher 2 Person who runs a course and grades Section 2 Ordered block of a course Activity 3 Something the learner does Submission 3 A learner's attempt at an activity Grade 3 Mark given to a submission Category 4 Catalogue classification of courses

docs.title: Rules to confirm
docs.text:
• A learner has at most one active enrolment per course.
  • A learner can submit only to a course in which the enrolment is active.
  • A grade is between zero and the activity's maximum grade.
  • A course is completed for a learner when all required activities have an accepted grade.
  • Only a teacher of the course can grade its submissions.
  • A cancelled enrolment keeps its submissions and grades.

docs.title: Actors and use cases
docs.text: Learner, Teacher, Manager and a notification system. The starting use cases are enrolInCourse, cancelEnrolment, submitActivity, gradeSubmission, completeCourse, publishCourse and reviewProgress, each with its package and the rules it touches.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text: The enrolment moves from active to cancelled or completed; whether a learner can re-enrol is a question the library asks.

docs.title: Questions it asks before use
docs.text:
1. Can a learner re-enrol after cancelling, or after failing?
  2. Is there a pass mark, and is it per activity or per course?
  3. Does grading allow several graders or a re-grade, and are previous grades kept?
  4. Is enrolment self-service, approved by a teacher or assigned by a manager?
  5. Is completion calculated or declared by a teacher?

docs.title: Stack packs
docs.text:
A stack pack fixes how reviewed models become code for one stack: the folder layout, the naming, the error handling, the persistence mapping and the test patterns. The agent reads the pack that matches targetStack before it plans code, and the pack takes precedence over the generic mapping of RUP to code.

Packs live in the packs folder of the Pro skill: a PACK.md and, where useful, fill-in skeletons.

docs.title: Included
docs.text:
Pack Stack nestjs-prisma TypeScript, NestJS, Prisma on PostgreSQL and Jest

More packs are announced in the Pro changelog.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
• Organised by feature package, one per concept of the domain model, with concrete classes. No layers of ports and abstract factories that the models do not ask for.
  • One class per file, the file named after the class; one reason to change per class.
  • A use case is one service; a controller only translates HTTP into a service call.
  • Dependencies are injected collaborators such as the Prisma service and the config service, never singletons.
  • Business rules live in entity methods or in the use-case service, never in the controller.

docs.title: What it generates per feature
docs.text: File Comes from Module and controller The boundary classes of the analysis Request and response objects The wireframe fields and the use-case card, validated with decorators One service per use case The design sequence, step by step Mapper Only where the response differs from the entity Unit test One test per flow and per rule

docs.title: From the data model to Prisma
docs.text:
Model Prisma Entity A model mapped to the table name of the data model Primary key A UUID unless the data model fixes another type Relation with multiplicity Relation fields on both sides, foreign key on the many side, cascade when the part cannot outlive the whole Unique rule @unique or @@unique Entity lifecycle An enum, with transitions guarded in the service Timestamps Created and updated columns

One migration per feature; an applied migration is never edited.

docs.title: Services, errors and tests
docs.text:
• A service validates the request, loads what the sequence loads in its order, applies the rules, throws a typed exception per failure path, persists inside one transaction when the sequence marks a boundary and returns the response.
  • Exceptions are mapped to HTTP in one filter.
  • Unit tests mock the persistence service; one test per main flow, alternative flow and rule, named with the identifier. End-to-end tests send one request per main flow.
  • Trace links are TSDoc tags (@rup UC-001 RF-001); no narrative comments elsewhere.

docs.title: Before it reports done
docs.text: It validates the Prisma schema, type-checks, runs the linter and the tests, and reports each result as it is. Anything it did not run is reported as unverified.

docs.title: RUP to code
docs.text:
From reviewed models, Pro generates code and tests that follow the conventions of your code base, with a link from each class or handler to the requirement and use case it implements.

Prompt
Use rup-flow-pro to implement UC-001 from the design.

docs.title: Preconditions
docs.text:
• The use cases to implement are at least reviewed. Drafts are listed and the agent asks before generating from them.
  • targetStack is set in the configuration. If it is empty the agent asks for the language, framework, persistence and testing, and saves the answers.
  • The output goes to codeRoot unless you pass another path; nothing is written outside the project.
  • Blocking items in the open questions that affect a use case stop the generation of that use case.

docs.title: How a model becomes code
docs.text:
Model element Code element Domain entity or design class Type or class with the same name; attributes from the dictionary Relation with multiplicity Typed reference or collection; foreign key in persistence Business rule RN-xxx Validation or domain method, with one test per rule Use case UC-xxx One application service or handler named after the use case <<boundary>> Controller, route or screen <<control>> and sequence Application service orchestrating the steps in the sequence order Repository interface Interface in the domain or application, implementation in persistence Data model table Migration plus mapping Specification states Branches and error results of the handler Wireframe fields Request and response contract and form fields Deployment Dockerfile, compose or manifests

A stack pack that matches your configuration refines this mapping for that stack.

docs.title: The run
docs.text:
1. The agent lists the files it will create or change per use case and shows the plan before writing when there are more than about five files.
  2. It creates the types and the persistence from the design data model.
  3. It implements each use case following its sequence step by step, including the failure paths of the specification.
  4. It generates tests: one per main flow, per alternative flow and per business rule. Test names cite the flow or rule identifier.

  5. It adds the trace link in the doc comment of each class or handler:

    /** Creates an order. @rup UC-001 RF-001 */

    The tag is traceTag in the configuration, @rup by default. 6. It runs the build, the tests and the linters of your project and reports the results as they are. 7. It updates the code map and the code and test columns of the traceability table. An artifact that was deliberately changed in code is set to sourceOfTruth: code, or the model is fixed; they are never left divergent.

docs.title: Rules the agent follows
docs.text:
• The conventions already present in the code base win over generic ones.
  • A decision the model does not contain stops the generation: the agent records a question and proposes options.
  • Nothing is generated beyond the requested use cases.
  • Code that could not be built or tested in the environment is reported as unverified.

docs.title: Subagents
docs.text:
For clients that support subagents, Pro includes two definitions in the agents folder of the skill. They split the work so that the review is not written by the one who wrote the documents.

Subagent Does Tools rup-architect Generates and updates the models, in any direction, and generates code from reviewed models Read, write, edit, search and shell rup-reviewer Read-only audit of the documentation and its alignment with the code Read and search only

docs.title: rup-architect
docs.text: It loads the Pro skill, reads the configuration, follows the workflow that matches the request (requirements to RUP, code to RUP, RUP to code or sync), marks every statement as confirmed, observed, assumed or open, writes only inside the documentation folder and the code folder, renders and checks before finishing, and ends with the files changed, the open questions, the checks it did not execute and the next step.

docs.title: rup-reviewer
docs.text: It applies the audit and sync guides. It cannot write files or run commands, so it states which checks it could not execute. It returns a table of findings with identifier, severity, evidence, impact and fix, and separates format defects, consistency defects, missing information, drift with the code and unexecuted checks. It does not rewrite artifacts.

docs.title: Installing them
docs.text: Copy the files of the skill's agents folder to the agents folder of your client, for Claude Code ~/.claude/agents or .claude/agents in a project. The definitions use the common frontmatter of name, description and tools.

docs.title: Without subagents
docs.text: An agent that has no subagents does the review as a separate pass after generating, following the audit guide, and keeps that pass read-only. Nothing else changes.

docs.title: Drift detection
docs.text:
Use it when documentation and code both exist and either may have moved. For every row of the traceability table and the code map, the agent checks:

  1. The cited code location exists.
  2. The entity attributes, relations and constraints in code match the dictionary and the data model.
  3. The handler of the use case follows the branches of the specification and the order of the sequence.
  4. The business rules are present, and tested.
  5. There is no code behaviour (endpoints, jobs, events) without a use case.

Each difference is classified:

Kind Meaning Default resolution Model ahead The model says something the code lacks Implement it, when the model is the source of truth Code ahead The code does something the model lacks Document it, when the code is the source of truth, otherwise ask Conflict Both exist and disagree Ask which is right and record a decision Dead Code or a model element nobody uses Report it; nothing is deleted without approval

sourceOfTruth decides the default direction and a conflict is never resolved silently. After resolving, both sides and the traceability row change in the same change, and each resolved conflict becomes a decision record. The output of a run is a table of differences with evidence and then the chosen action, never a rewrite of everything.

docs.title: Audit
docs.text:
A review of the documentation and its alignment with the code. It is read-only unless you ask for fixes.

Dimension Looks for Completeness Requirements without a use case, use cases without a requirement, realization, wireframes or specification Consistency Names, attributes and rules that differ between domain, use cases, analysis, design and data model Domain hierarchy Levels without justification, everything at level 1, relations that contradict the levels Behaviour Flows without failure paths, preconditions not checked, unreachable states Traceability Empty cells, reused identifiers, code-map locations that do not exist Non-functional Requirements without a measure, missing security or permission rules Diagrams Missing SVG, syntax errors, crossing lines, unreadable labels, too many elements Provenance Assumptions written as facts, rules without a source Drift Differences with the code

docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
| ID | Severity | Finding | Evidence | Impact | Fix | Status |

Severity is blocker (the artifact cannot be trusted or built), major (wrong or missing content) or minor (style, clarity). Evidence is a file path and the quoted element; there is no finding without evidence.

docs.title: What the audit never claims
docs.text: It never states that the project is "complete RUP", that the UML is semantically correct or that a diagram is clean unless it was inspected. It states what was checked and how, and lists the checks that were not executed, for example the visual inspection of the rendered images.

docs.text:

  • In the domain model, each level package is tagged <<level1>> to <<level4>> in PlantUML (:::level1 in Mermaid) and the renderer colors it from levels.
  • Stereotypes such as <<boundary>>, <<control>> and <<entity>> are content and stay.
  • Wireframes are PlantUML salt layouts and are not themed.

docs.title: Use-case cards
docs.text:
In the free edition a use case has one card, the requirements card. In Pro it has one card per discipline, so the story of a use case can be followed from the requirement to the test.

Card Folder Holds Requirements 01-requirements/use-cases/<name> Actor, goal, flows, rules, specification, wireframes Analysis 02-analysis/use-cases/<name> Participating classes with one responsibility each, collaboration Design 03-design/use-cases/<name> The elements that realize it, sequence, failure path Implementation 04-implementation/use-cases/<name> Code locations, tests table

RUP new use-case <name> creates all four, assigns the next identifier, adds the row to the traceability table and refreshes the index.

docs.title: One navigation table
docs.text:
Every card of a use case starts with the same table, so you move between disciplines without hunting for files:

| Overview | Requirements | Analysis | Design | Implementation | Tests |

The current discipline is bold, the others are links, Overview opens the general use-case diagram and Tests opens the tests table of the implementation card. The table is generated; do not retype it.

docs.title: The index
docs.text: The requirements README holds, between rup-flow:use-cases markers, a generated table with the identifier, use case, actors, package, requirement, links to the three realization cards and the status. Below it are the use-case diagrams: one general diagram, and one per actor when there are several. RUP index regenerates all of it after a card's front matter changes, and check warns when it is stale.

docs.title: Front matter that drives the diagrams
docs.text:
Key Effect actor Comma separated; each actor is drawn outside the system boundary package Groups related use cases inside the boundary includes, extends Drawn as <<include>> and <<extend>> relations

An actor is linked only to the use cases that no other use case of that actor includes, as is usual in use-case diagrams.

docs.title: Checklist before marking reviewed
docs.text:
• The main flow reaches the goal and each step has a system response.
  • Failure and alternative paths exist for each input and precondition.
  • Entities, attributes and rules referenced exist in the domain model.
  • The wireframes cover the fields of the flow.
  • The row exists in the traceability table.

docs.title: Pro versions and compatibility

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
Run the CLI from the project root. RUP below stands for node <skill-dir>/scripts/rup.mjs, where <skill-dir> is the folder that contains SKILL.md.

RUP <command> [arguments] [flags]

Commands and flags marked Pro exist only in the Pro edition. In the free edition they stop with a message that names Pro and exit with code 1.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Command Edition Effect init Free Create rup.config.json and the documentation skeleton. Never overwrites a file. new use-case <camelName> Free Scaffold the cards of a use case, then refresh the index. Free: requirements card and specification. Pro: also analysis, design and implementation cards, wireframes, collaboration and sequence. index Free Regenerate the use-case index from the cards. Pro: also the use-case diagrams. render Free Draw every .puml source into a .svg through the PlantUML server. Pro: themed, plus Mermaid and PNG. check Free Verify structure, links and diagrams. Pro: also traceability and realization checks. editions Free Print the catalogue and what the installation includes. version Free Print the edition and version, --json for machines. instructions --target <t> Free Add or refresh the rup-flow block in an agent instruction file. server up / server down Free Start or stop the PlantUML container. health Free Verify that the PlantUML server renders. config Free Print the resolved configuration. explore Pro Build explorer.html, the interactive viewer of every diagram. themes Pro List the palettes, --json for machines. scan Pro Inventory of the code base, the input of code to RUP.

Without a command the CLI prints its usage.

docs.title: Common flags
docs.text: Flag Meaning --root <dir> Project root. Defaults to the current directory. --out <dir> Documentation directory, relative to the root (overrides outDir). --lang <code> Language of the documents (overrides docLanguage). --project <name> Project name used in titles. --code-root <dir> Where the code lives (overrides codeRoot). --plantuml-url <url> Address of the PlantUML server. --force Redraw diagrams that are up to date.

docs.title: Pro flags Pro
docs.text: Flag Meaning --theme <preset> Palette: default, ocean, forest, sunset, grape, mono, dark or high-contrast. --color-<name> "#RRGGBB" Override one color: background, text, line, border, primary, secondary, accent or note. --font <name>, --font-size <n> Font family and size of the diagrams. --diagram-language plantuml\|mermaid Language of the diagram sources. --outputs svg,png,html What render produces: SVG, PNG previews, the explorer. --preview-png Add PNG previews to the outputs.

docs.title: init
docs.text:
RUP init --out docs/rup --lang es --project shop

Creates the configuration and the skeleton. Files that exist are skipped. The report lists what was created; in the free edition it also says how many artifacts are available in Pro.

docs.title: new use-case
docs.text:
RUP new use-case createOrder --title "Create order" --actor Customer --package Ordering --goal "Place an order"
Flag Meaning --title <text> Title of the card. Defaults to the name. --actor <names> Actors, comma separated. Defaults to Actor. --package <name> Package. Defaults to General. --goal <text> The goal in one sentence. --requirement <id> Requirement identifier. Defaults to RF-001. --includes <names>, --extends <names> Names of related use cases. --id <UC-xxx> Force the identifier instead of the next free one. --discipline <list> Pro Which cards to create: requirements,analysis,design,implementation.

The name must be camelCase made of letters and digits. The command fails otherwise. Pro also adds the row of the use case to the traceability table.

docs.title: render
docs.text:
RUP render --path docs/rup/00-domain-model --force
Flag Meaning --path <dir> Render only this directory. --force Redraw everything.

A change of palette redraws everything automatically. The exit code is 1 when any diagram fails.

docs.title: check
docs.text: --strict makes warnings fail the command. Without it, only errors do. What it reports is listed in Render and check diagrams.

docs.title: explore Pro
docs.text: Writes explorer.html in the documentation directory: one file, no server, no network. Use --outputs svg,html to build it after every render. The features are in The interactive explorer.

docs.title: scan Pro
docs.text:
RUP scan --code-root src --write

Prints, or with --write saves as 04-implementation/code-inventory.json, the extensions, manifests and the candidate entities, entry points, services, persistence, tests and contracts of the code. --limit <n> caps each sample (60 by default). The agent reads it to start code to RUP.

docs.title: instructions
docs.text:
RUP instructions --target agents,claude,gemini

Without --target it lists the targets. --skill-path <dir> sets where the block says the skill lives. All targets are in Compatible agents.

docs.text:
RUP version
RUP editions --json

version prints rup-flow free 1.0.0, or for Pro rup-flow Pro 1.0.0 (built on rup-flow free 1.0.0). With --json it prints the edition and versions as JSON. editions prints the catalogue as a checklist of what the installation includes.

docs.text: Needs Docker with Compose. The port comes from plantuml.url.

docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Done. 1 A check failed, a render failed, or the command stopped (invalid input, missing server, a capability that is part of Pro).

docs.title: Sources and renders
docs.text: Every diagram is a .puml source with its .svg next to it. Markdown links to the SVG with a relative path. .rup-render-state.json in the documentation directory records the last render so unchanged diagrams are skipped.

docs.title: Front matter
docs.text:
Every Markdown artifact except the index READMEs starts with a block like this:

---
id: UC-001
name: createOrder
title: Create order
actor: Customer
package: Ordering
status: draft
origin: requirements
sourceOfTruth: model
requirement: RF-001
includes: validateStock
extends:
---
Key Values Meaning id UC-001 and so on Stable identifier name camelCase Use-case folder name title text Human title actor names, comma separated Primary actors package text Group of related use cases status draft, reviewed, approved Review state; never promoted by the agent origin requirements Where the content came from sourceOfTruth model The model leads; code, if any, must follow it requirement RF-001 Requirement the use case serves includes, extends use-case names Relations drawn in use-case diagrams

The use-case index and check read id, title, actor, package, status, requirement, includes and extends.

docs.title: Identifiers
docs.text:
Prefix Meaning RF-001 Functional requirement RNF-001 Non-functional requirement UC-001 Use case RN-001 Business rule Q-001 Open question

Never reuse or renumber an identifier. Mark a withdrawn one retired. The prefixes come from ids in the configuration.

docs.title: Provenance marks
docs.text:
Every statement in a document carries one provenance. This is what keeps the documentation honest.

Mark Meaning Who sets it confirmed You said it The agent, only for what you stated observed Found in the code, cited as path:line The agent, when it reads code (Pro) assumed Proposed by the agent The agent open A question The agent, in open-questions.md

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
1. An assumption is never presented as confirmed.
  2. An unknown business rule goes to open-questions.md, not into the model.
  3. The agent never invents permissions, rules, states or attributes to make a document look complete.
  4. An assumed item stays assumed until you confirm it.

docs.title: In practice
docs.text:
The entity dictionary and the business-rule table have a Source column. A rule without a source is assumed. Open questions record who asked, when and what they block.

Observed claims need code, which is the job of the code-to-RUP workflow in rup-flow Pro. In the free edition, statements are confirmed, assumed or open.

First release of the free edition from a clean history. It turns requirements into a basic RUP documentation set with PlantUML diagrams for any coding agent.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• The simplified domain model, actors, requirements, the use-case requirements card with its specification statechart, the analysis classes and the open-questions list.
  • The CLI: init, new use-case, index, render, check, instructions, server, health, config, editions and version.
  • editions.json: a catalogue of every diagram, document, workflow and tool, marked free or Pro. The CLI loads scripts/pro/index.mjs when it exists next to it and stops with a message that names Pro for anything outside the edition.
  • Instruction targets for fifteen kinds of agent: AGENTS.md, Claude, Gemini, Copilot, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, Roo Code, Kilo Code, Continue, JetBrains Junie, Amazon Q Developer, Zed, Aider and a portable file for any agent with a shell.
  • install.mjs --dir <folder> installs the skill into the skills folder of any client.
  • Versioned release packages: rup-flow-free-<version>.zip.

docs.title: Update rup-flow
docs.text: Your documentation and rup.config.json live in your project. The skill lives in its own folder, so updating it never rewrites your documents.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Read the changelog for the versions you skipped: free and, for Pro, Pro.
  2. Download the new package, rup-flow-free-<version>.zip or rup-flow-pro-<version>.zip.
  3. Unzip it over the old skill folder, or replace the folder. Keep the same skills folder your agent already reads.
  4. Run RUP version to confirm the version and RUP check on a project.
  5. Run RUP index once; the use-case index is regenerated from the cards.

On Claude on the web, upload the new ZIP in Customize → Skills.

docs.title: Agents that read an instruction file
docs.text:
Run instructions again for each target. It replaces only the delimited block, so the rest of the file stays as you wrote it:

RUP instructions --target cursor,windsurf

docs.title: From the 0.x releases
docs.text: Earlier releases of rup-flow were distributed differently and included features that are now part of rup-flow Pro: themes, Mermaid, the explorer, code scanning, design, implementation and traceability artifacts. Version 1.0 starts a clean line with two editions. Files you generated before stay in your project and the free check keeps working on them; to keep producing those artifacts, use rup-flow Pro.

docs.title: Versioning and URLs
docs.text:
Four numbers answer four different questions:

  • Free version: which release of the free skill is installed?
  • Pro version: which release of rup-flow Pro, and which free version does it contain?
  • Documentation line: which compatible MAJOR.MINOR contract describes it?
  • Publication revision: which approved snapshot of these pages produced the current wording and images?

docs.title: Reading your own version
docs.text:
RUP version
rup-flow free 1.0.0

RUP version
rup-flow Pro 1.0.0 (built on rup-flow free 1.0.0)

The same number is in the name of the package, rup-flow-free-1.0.0.zip or rup-flow-pro-1.0.0.zip, and in the metadata.version of SKILL.md.

docs.title: How the editions map
docs.text:
Pro Contains free Read the docs of line 1.0.x 1.0.x 1.0

A Pro release is documented on the line of the free version it contains. Pro pages carry the Pro version since which a capability exists, so one site covers both editions.

docs.title: MAJOR.MINOR controls the site
docs.text:
The version selector and the canonical address use the free edition's MAJOR.MINOR. Compatible patches update the same line instead of creating a new copy of the site.

Edition line:      1.0.x
Validated version: 1.0.0
Version selector:  1.0
Canonical path:    /rup-flow-docs/1.0/

docs.title: Aliases
docs.text:
Alias Points to latest The newest documented line stable The newest documented line that is not a preview

The site root redirects to latest.

docs.title: Publication revisions
docs.text: Each approved publication of these pages gets an immutable tag and a GitHub release. A later editorial fix is a new revision in the same line; it never rewrites an earlier one.
